## Catastrophes and hidden information

Catastrophes are seeded, rare, and fully visible only to the power they strike, which turns them into diplomatic material.

**Types (prototype).** Drought and famine (income falls), plague (units and income lost), flood, and earthquake (a province damaged for several turns).

**Asymmetric knowledge.** The affected power sees the exact damage. Everyone else hears of it later and vaguely, through envoys, spies and rumor.

**Why it matters.** "Our harvest failed, so we cannot pay the tribute this year" might be true or a convenient lie. Neighbors must decide whether to believe it, help, or exploit the weakness, and may pay a spy to find out.

The letters record exactly this move: the king of Alashiya excused a small copper shipment because "the hand of Nergal", the god of plague, had killed his men.

**Hidden by default.** Beyond catastrophes, treasuries, unit counts outside sight, contracts and characters' secrets are all private. Players see their own land and what borders it as it is now. News of distant provinces, including who holds them, travels like everything else and arrives late (pillar 4); the rest is whatever their people bring home.

**Information as an asset** (decided 19 October 2026). News is structured, so it shows in the visuals and the game's tracking, and characters sell what they know ("Information as a structured asset" and "Characters as sellers of news" in the Ideas tab; build order items 7 and 11).
